result.strongest_objection: Rule 2 specifies that `distance_ly` 'must be absent' when targeting Sol or an invalid catalogue entry, which ensures an incomplete check and creates a false-negative vulnerability: if `b.context.client.map` omits `distance_ly` on a valid non-Sol target, the leaf-walk in `check_context` will never visit `client.map.distance_ly` unless the presence requirement is explicitly inverted and enforced against `view.journey.plan.target`.
result.catch: In addition to the missing presence check for `distance_ly`, Rule 3 allowlists `client.map.hold_s` (`HOLD_S`), `client.archive.` (`unlocked_count`), and `client.crew.` (`working`) without any value verification, even though the clause-4 display gate requires proving every number on screen equals `format(state[field])` and all three are numeric fields.
result.proposed_fix: 1. In Design §2, specify that `check_context` also checks required presence: if `b.context` has `client.map` and `view.journey.plan.target` resolves to a catalogue entry with `dist_ly`, require `b.context.client.map.has("distance_ly")` (failing `context-source <node> client.map.distance_ly` if missing), and if it does not resolve (e.g., Sol), fail if `distance_ly` is present. 2. In Design §2/§3, verify `client.map.hold_s == GalaxyMap.HOLD_S` as a source rule rather than allowlisting it unchecked, and either add a source rule or explicitly document why `client.archive.unlocked_count` and `client.crew.working` cannot be cross-checked against console state or why they are exempt from clause 4.
